    Why Runvis

    You don’t need
    another running watch

    People say you need a dedicated watch, like a Garmin or a COROS, to see training load or recovery time. But the sensors behind those numbers are already in the Apple Watch on your wrist.

    The sensors are already on your wrist

    Heart rate, GPS, cadence, elevation. Newer models also measure ground contact time and vertical oscillation.

    The formulas are public

    Training load, recovery time, and threshold estimates come from published formulas used widely in sports science. Runvis runs them right on your watch and iPhone.

    The missing piece was a coach

    Someone to read the numbers, decide what you do today, and talk to you while you run. Runvis fills that spot.

    Today’s decision

    Wake up to today’s workout,
    already picked for you

    It checks last night’s sleep, HRV, resting heart rate, and yesterday’s training load against your own 28-day range. Then it picks today’s workout and tells you why in one line.

    You don’t even have to look at your watch. Say “Hey Siri, what should I run today with Runvis?” and it reads you today’s decision. Ask about your readiness or this week’s plan the same way.

    The decision first, the reasons right below

    Today’s workout sits at the top of the screen, with the reasons right below it. Everything else is further down, for reference. Tap any number to see what it means, how it’s calculated, and your usual range.

    • On an off day, it dials the intensity down and tells you why
    • Still want the original workout? You can run it.
    • When there’s not enough data, it shows “Learning” instead of a number
    Today’s decisionYour readiness ring and today’s workout, right on your wrist.

    After the run

    Once you’re done,
    see the why, not just the numbers

    Splits, heart rate zones, running dynamics, and a one-line coaching note are free. Subscribe and you also get Coach’s Record Radar, which finds your fastest stretches inside a run, plus a lactate threshold estimate and this week’s distance budget.

    Workout detail reportFree

    Pace by split, heart rate zone breakdown, average cadence and ground contact time, and one line from your coach about this run.

    Body reportFree

    Readiness, sleep, HRV, resting heart rate, VO₂ max. Tap one to open its trend chart and your usual 28-day range.

    Coach’s Record Radar (fastest segments · PR book)Subscription

    Not your finish times. It picks out your fastest 1K, 5K, 10K, and half-marathon stretches from inside your runs over the last 90 days, and shows how they compare with your previous records.

    Lactate threshold estimateSubscription

    It takes your best 30-minute stretch from at least 2 runs in the last 90 days and estimates your threshold pace and heart rate from them. If you’ve entered your max heart rate, only stretches held at 85% of it or more count.

    What if there’s no 30-minute stretch?

    Then it uses a 20-minute stretch. If there isn’t one of those either, it estimates from the average of 3 runs of 20 minutes or longer at 85% or more of your max heart rate. That method only works if you’ve entered your max heart rate. Whichever method it uses, the screen always tells you.

    Coach’s BrakeSubscription

    It sets this week’s distance budget from your last 4 weeks of training. Tell it something hurts, and it trims the budget.

    Runvis Fitness IndexSubscription

    Worked backward from your fastest splits, your Fitness Index predicts your time at each distance. See it side by side with your Apple Watch VO₂ max.

    If it’s an estimate, we say so. Without enough data, a metric stays at “Learning.” Anything we couldn’t stand behind, we left out from the start.

    Tap any metric to see it next to your usual range

    Race prep

    Week by week to race day.
    Segment by segment on the day.

    Enter your goal race and goal time, and you get a week-by-week roadmap to race day. It’ll also tell you honestly whether that goal fits your current fitness. Viewing the plan is free. Having the coach lead you through each segment on the watch is part of the subscription.

    Pick a coach, and the plan and the tone change with it

    Finish First, Balanced, or PR Chase. Pick one, and both your training mix and the coach’s tone on the run change with it. If you’re just starting out, no coach will give you intervals that push too hard.

    • Your coach leads every interval segment, then scores you against the plan
    • On a rough day, one tap dials the intensity down and reworks the plan
    • Back after 14 or more days off? For 2 weeks, weekly distance restarts at 55%→75% of your 4-week average before the break (45%→65% after 28 days or more). The first run is 20 minutes, and week 3 is your usual plan again. “Keep this week as planned” turns it off for that week, and it’s free
    • No race times yet? That’s fine. One 12-minute test run on the watch gives you your first plan

    A coach who knows the course ahead of time

    Load the race course GPX and it knows where the climbs begin before you get there. Send grade-adjusted segment paces and fueling points to your watch, and on race day, just follow the cues.

    • One recent result gives you predicted times and goal paces for the 5K, 10K, half, and full marathon
    • Run the same course again and your best becomes a ghost, showing how far ahead or behind you are
    • From 9 days out, your predicted time factors in the race-day forecast

    Privacy

    No account, no server,
    so the coach talks in tunnels.

    Recording, analysis, and coaching all happen on your watch and iPhone, and Runvis never uploads your workout or health records anywhere. Here’s what does go in and out. For weather and course forecasts, Runvis sends Apple your coordinates rounded to about 1 km; for neighborhood names in your workout list, each run’s start point rounded to about 100 m. For the name of the neighborhood you’re in right now and for auto-generated routes, it sends your current coordinates, not rounded. Maps come from Apple Maps, just for the area on your screen, and the App Store handles payments. The public course and shoe lists are download-only, and the running shoe search page opens only when the app is in Korean and you tap its link yourself on your iPhone’s Shoes screen. Exactly what goes where is set out here: Privacy Policy

    Or skip the subscription: a ₩59,000 lifetime pass. It’s a launch price, and if the price goes up later, nothing changes for people who already bought. At Korean App Store prices, it pays for itself in about 2 years compared with the ₩29,000 yearly plan, or about 15 months compared with ₩3,900 monthly.     When do the numbers fill in?

    All 8 deep analyses unlock the moment you pay. The numbers fill in as your runs add up, and until then each one tells you what it still needs.

    • Lactate Threshold (est.): 2 stretches of 30 minutes (or 20) held at 85% or more of your max heart rate. If you only have runs without a route, it works from your entered max heart rate plus 3 runs of 20 minutes or longer.
    • Endurance training volume: 6 or more runs across 3 of the last 4 weeks, with at least 2 weeks between your first and last run.
    • Hill exposure: 2 runs with climbing.
    • Heat exposure index: 3 runs on days above 22°C.
    • Intensity mix: 8 days of data, including 5 runs with heart rate.
    • Coach's Brake: 2 weeks of runs.
    • Coach's Record Radar: records start showing up after a single run of 1 km or more.
    • Leg Load: a value appears from your first run with distance recorded.

    FAQ

    Before you start

    Can I use it without a watch?

    Yes. Your iPhone alone records your run with GPS and calls out your split pace every 1 km (every 1 mile if you use miles). Without a subscription, an iPhone-only run gives you those split calls, plus the run-walk switch calls when you run one of the 3 starter guides. With a subscription, the iPhone coaches your pace too, and heart rate zone cues come through only when you connect a Bluetooth heart rate strap (any standard BLE strap, like a Polar H10 or Wahoo TICKR), since the iPhone has no heart rate sensor. Form coaching, hill warnings, and off-route alerts only work when you run with the watch.

    Which Apple Watch do I need?

    watchOS 10 or later (Apple Watch Series 4 or later) and iOS 17 or later. Heart rate and GPS are all it needs. On newer models that measure ground contact time and vertical oscillation, form coaching gets more detailed. On models that don’t, it coaches from cadence.

    What happens to my runs if I cancel?

    Your runs stay right where they are, in Apple Health. After you cancel, recording, plan viewing, and the workout detail report stay free.

    Can I start with no running history?

    Yes. Do one 12-minute test run on the watch and you’ll get estimated 5K and 10K times and your first plan the same day. The test is watch-only. With just an iPhone, you get GPS recording, split pace cues, and plan viewing from day one, and your plan starts from your recent weekly distance. If Apple Health already has your history, the screen right after you connect it shows your last 90 days in real numbers (weekly distance, fastest run, HRV range), and with enough past HRV and 4 weeks of workouts, Readiness and the load spike warning start on day one. With no history, Readiness needs nights of sleep with the watch on, so it usually shows up after about 2 weeks. The load spike warning (ACWR) takes about 4. Efficiency vs Baseline appears once you’ve entered your max heart rate and logged 3 runs over 10 minutes with heart rate, all at the same intensity (easy, moderate, or hard). For the first few, you’re compared against a baseline that doesn’t yet account for intensity or when the reading was taken, and the screen tells you so.

    Lifetime or yearly: which is the better deal?

    The lifetime pass is a one-time purchase with no auto-renewal. It pays for itself in about 2 years compared with yearly, or about 15 months compared with monthly. If you plan to use Runvis longer than that, lifetime costs less. It’s also the only plan that works with Apple Family Sharing. Monthly and yearly subscriptions aren’t eligible.

    What happens when I switch devices?

    Your runs are saved in Apple Health, so the Health app on your new device brings them over. What lived only in Runvis (your profile, heart rate zones, shoe list, and the baselines your coach has built) goes into a single file from Settings → Data → “Export my data.” On the new device, bring it back with “Restore from backup.” The file stays wherever you save it. Runvis doesn’t send it anywhere. Your subscription comes back through the App Store with “Restore Purchases.”
